---
title: "Skills and deterministic tools"
---

A tool is an executable capability such as reading a file or running a shell command. A skill is scoped guidance that helps an agent use a capability reliably for a recurring task. A script or test is often preferable when the desired behaviour is deterministic.

Each exercise ships a repository-scoped R binary-package skill. It documents the Linux/P3M installation path and its limits; it is not a license to install arbitrary packages or use real data. Inspect its trigger and scope in `.agents/skills/r-binary-packages/SKILL.md` before asking an agent to use it.

Skill creation is optional. First identify a safe repeated task, try a one-off prompt, then promote only the stable knowledge. Run a new case and revise the skill from observed behaviour. Different harnesses discover skills in different directories; the Claude copy is intentionally real and synchronized rather than a symlink.
